analysis.title: Alger on the Money: Fall Harvesting
key_insights: Stocks down more than 10% in a calendar year through October (tax loss candidates, TLCs) have outperformed the S&P 500 by an average of 1.7% from November through January, based on Bank of America analysis covering January 1986 through January 2026.
More than 110 stocks in the S&P 500 are down over 10% YTD as of October 2026, so tax-loss selling could be significant in the coming weeks, even though the index has strong YTD returns.
Mutual funds typically realize losses before October 31, the deadline for most to realize capital gains, and retail investors typically sell by December 31.

Some of the worst-performing S&P 500 stocks YTD are rate-sensitive names that fell as interest rates rose. Alger says investors rotating out of them may have sold companies poised to grow strongly once the rate headwind subsides.
Alger sees the opportunity as most pronounced in rate-sensitive industries such as housing, automotive and consumer finance, where multiples have compressed despite market share gains.
November and December have historically been among the strongest months for US stocks, which Alger cites as supportive timing as tax-related selling fades and investors refocus on fundamentals.
